extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML sections, figures, source tables, and supplementary PDF text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TI and cTI directly bind model lipid membranes and induce vesicle leakage in vitro; negatively charged POPC/POPS membranes show stronger interaction/leakage than neutral POPC in the source tables.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TI and cTI as representatives of parent and cyclic tachyplesin peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model membrane assays support membrane interaction and leakage, not a complete in-cell killing pathway for every peptide.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Tryptophan fluorescence partitioning and quenching assays support peptide insertion/orientation within lipid bilayers, with cyclic analogues showing more protected/deeper Trp insertion in negatively charged model membranes.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TI-TIII and cTI-cTIII, with TI/cTI depth quenching in Table 9

mechanism_claims.limitations: Orientation is inferred from biophysical quenching and model membranes; it should not be upgraded to direct bacterial cell-wall or apoptosis mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports antimicrobial, antibiofilm, hemolytic, and cancer-cell cytotoxic phenotypes; these are activity outcomes and should be interpreted separately from the membrane-mechanism assays.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Membrane binding/leakage and Trp insertion are direct in vitro model-membrane assays, not direct proof of full bacterial/cancer-cell killing pathway.
MIC, biofilm CC50, hemolysis, and cell-line CC50 are retained as activity records, not mechanism claims.
